mainTopic: The story of שמעיה ואבטליון, the משנה of the eight בגדי כהונה, and the number of strands in the priestly threads
overview: This amud opens with the last words of a פסוק from איוב that closes the previous אגדתא. The גמרא then quotes the משנה's line that the כהן גדול made a celebration for his friends. It brings a ברייתא about a כהן גדול who insulted שמעיה ואבטליון for coming from converts, and they answered that true descent from אהרן is measured by acting like אהרן. A new משנה teaches that the כהן גדול serves in eight garments and a regular כהן in four, and that the אורים ותומים are consulted only for the king, the אב בית דין, or someone the community needs. The גמרא brings a ברייתא listing how many strands go into each thread of the בגדי כהונה. It derives the six-strand rule from the repeated word שש, and proves that שש means linen in two ways: from the word בד and from a פסוק in יחזקאל, which is explained as an old tradition that יחזקאל attached to a verse. Next, the גמרא shows that the pomegranate threads have eight strands each, learned from the אבנט, with two further reasons given by רב מרי and רב אשי. Finally, it begins to give the source for the twelve strands of the מעיל, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the verse about water making a tree blossom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a פסוק from איוב that supports the previous teaching about joining a family of תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "From the scent of water it will blossom, and it will put forth branches like a plant."
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of a פסוק that the גמרא used on the previous amud. A tree that seems dried up can blossom again when it is near water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water is a משל for תורה. Even if a person's family line has dried up from lack of תורה, joining a family of תלמידי חכמים can help his children grow into scholars. This step only finishes the earlier ראיה. It does not begin a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: From the scent of water, a משל for the closeness of תורה

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the previous discussion, which started on the previous amud. Do not try to connect it to the story or the משנה that follow.

phrases.english: from the scent of water it will blossom
and put forth branches like a plant.
phrases.notes: קָצִיר here means branches, not harvest

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a פסוק cited earlier
steps.raayaObject: Joining a family of תלמידי חכמים brings תורה to one's children

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the כהן גדול made a celebration
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about the כהן גדול making a celebration for his friends after יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he would make a holiday celebration for his loved ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes words from the משנה as a heading. This is a setup line that prepares for the ברייתא coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the כהן גדול made a party because he came out of the קודש הקדשים safely. The גמרא will now tell a story about a כהן גדול leaving the בית המקדש, which connects to this scene.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means a festive celebration, not a holiday like פסח or סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: Here יום טוב means a party. It does not mean a holiday like פסח or סוכות.

phrases.english: And he would make a feast for his loved ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to the words of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול held a celebration for his friends after leaving the בית המקדש safely

steps.title: The crowd leaves the כהן גדול to follow שמעיה ואבטליון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a כהן גדול leaving the בית המקדש with everyone following him, until the people saw שמעיה ואבטליון and followed them instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There was an incident with a certain כהן גדול who left the בית המקדש, and everyone walked after him. When they saw שמעיה ואבטליון, they left him and walked after שמעיה ואבטליון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a story. The crowd that was escorting the כהן גדול switches to escorting the great sages שמעיה ואבטליון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people showed more honor to the leading תלמידי חכמים than to the כהן גדול. This sets up the tension in the next step, where the כהן גדול reacts with jealousy.

keyTerms.meaning: The heads of the סנהדרין and teachers of הלל and שמאי

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There was an incident with one High Priest
who left the Holy Temple
and everyone was walking after him.
Once they saw Shemaya and Avtalyon,
they left him by himself
and walked after Shemaya and Avtalyon.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story connected to the משנה's scene of the כהן גדול leaving the בית המקדש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people gave greater honor to the תלמידי חכמים than to the כהן גדול

steps.title: The כהן גדול insults the sages for coming from converts
steps.stepSummary: When שמעיה ואבטליון come to take leave of him, the כהן גדול greets them with a mocking line about their descent from non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, שמעיה ואבטליון came to take leave of the כהן גדול. He said to them: "Let the descendants of the nations come in peace."
steps.whatsHappening: The sages politely come to say goodbye, and the jealous כהן גדול insults them. His greeting reminds everyone that they came from converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface it sounds like a blessing of peace, but it is really a put-down. His point is that you are not real Jews like me, a son of אהרן. This sets up their sharp answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of the nations, meaning of non-Jewish ancestry

steps.confusionAlert: The words sound friendly, but they are an insult. שמעיה ואבטליון descended from converts.

phrases.english: Eventually Shemaya and Avtalyon came
to take leave of the High Priest.
He said to them:
Let the descendants of the nations come in peace.
phrases.notes: A mocking reference to their descent from converts

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The כהן גדול reacts with jealousy to the honor the sages received
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול belittles the sages because of their lineage

steps.title: The sages answer that acting like אהרן is what counts
steps.stepSummary: שמעיה ואבטליון turn the insult around: descendants of converts who act like אהרן deserve peace, while a son of אהרן who does not act like him does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: "Let the descendants of the nations come in peace, since they do the deeds of אהרן. But let the son of אהרן not come in peace, since he does not do the deeds of אהרן."
steps.whatsHappening: The sages reject the כהן גדול's assumption that family lineage makes a person greater. They answer him with his own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן was known as אוהב שלום ורודף שלום, someone who loved and pursued peace. The sages, who bring peace, are the true followers of אהרן. The כהן גדול, who insults people, has abandoned אהרן's ways despite his lineage.

keyTerms.meaning: The deeds of אהרן, meaning loving and pursuing peace
A descendant of אהרן, a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Real greatness comes from acting like אהרן, not only from being born into his family. A convert's descendant who pursues peace stands above a כהן גדול who insults people.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story teaches the value of גרים and their descendants, and that honor follows Torah and good deeds rather than lineage alone.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Let the descendants of the nations come in peace
who perform the deeds of Aaron,
and let not a descendant of Aaron come in peace
who does not perform the deeds of Aaron.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: יֵיתוֹן בְּנֵי עַמְמִין לִשְׁלָם דְּעָבְדִין עוֹבָדָא דְאַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers and overturns the insult
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the כהן גדול's whole claim that lineage alone gives worth
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He measured greatness by birth instead of by following אהרן's peace-loving deeds

steps.title: The eight garments of the כהן גדול and the four of a regular כהן
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a regular כהן serves in four garments, and the כהן גדול adds four more, for eight in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The כהן גדול serves in eight garments, and a regular כהן in four: a tunic, trousers, a turban, and a belt. The כהן גדול adds to these a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, and a forehead plate.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and lists the בגדי כהונה. Four garments belong to every כהן, and four extra belong only to the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The regular כהן's four are כתונת, מכנסים, מצנפת, and אבנט. The כהן גדול wears those four plus חושן, אפוד, מעיל, and ציץ. These eight are his year-round garments, which differ from the white garments he wears for the special עבודה of יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: Here הדיוט does not mean a simpleton. It means an ordinary כהן.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The High Priest serves in eight garments,
and the common priest in four:
in a tunic, trousers, a mitre, and a belt.
The High Priest adds beyond him:
a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, and a frontplate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול serves in eight garments and a regular כהן in four

steps.title: Who may consult the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the אורים ותומים are consulted when the כהן גדול wears these garments, and only for the king, the אב בית דין, or someone the community needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: In these garments the אורים ותומים are consulted. They are consulted only for a king, for the head of the court, or for someone the community needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that the כהן גדול must wear all eight garments to ask questions through the אורים ותומים. It also limits who may ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אורים ותומים were in the חושן, so the full set of garments is needed. Private people cannot ask about personal matters. Only public leaders, or someone whose question affects the community, may ask.

keyTerms.meaning: The Divine Names placed in the חושן, used to receive answers from השם
The head or president of the court

steps.whatToRemember: The אורים ותומים work only when the כהן גדול wears all eight garments, and only for public needs: the king, the אב בית דין, or someone the community needs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the אורים ותומים served the nation's needs, not personal curiosity. That sets up the גמרא's coming discussion of the garments and how the inquiry worked.

phrases.english: In these, the Urim VeTummim are consulted.
And they are consulted only for a king,
and for the president of the court,
and for one whom the community needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a law that depends on the eight garments just listed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אורים ותומים are consulted only in the eight garments, and only for the king, the אב בית דין, or someone the community needs

steps.title: How many strands go into each thread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that lists how many strands are twisted into the threads of each priestly garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Sages taught: items described as שש have threads doubled six times. Items described as משזר have eight. The מעיל has twelve. The פרוכת has twenty-four. The חושן and אפוד have twenty-eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה's garments by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives the strand count for each type of thread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שש means linen, but it also means 'six', so the ברייתא reads it as 'six strands'. Each garment that gets fancier also gets a thicker thread: eight, twelve, twenty-four, and twenty-eight strands.

keyTerms.meaning: Linen, and also the number six
Their thread is doubled, meaning made of multiple strands

steps.confusionAlert: שש here is a double word: it names the material (linen) and also hints at the number of strands (six). The rest of the sugya depends on both meanings.

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Sages taught:
Items about which 'shesh' is stated
their thread is doubled six-fold.
'Twined' means eight.
The robe: twelve.
The curtain: twenty-four.
The breastplate and ephod: twenty-eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה of the eight garments (step 6) by giving the thread details.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Thread counts: שש = 6, משזר = 8, מעיל = 12, פרוכת = 24, חושן and אפוד = 28.

steps.title: Where do we learn the six-strand rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that threads called שש are made of six strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: That their thread is doubled six-fold, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's first rule. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שש could simply name the material. The גמרא wants to know what tells us that it also requires six strands.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: That their thread is doubled six-fold, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's first rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the six-strand requirement.

steps.title: The verse that repeats the word linen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing the priestly garments, where the word for linen appears over and over.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And they made the tunics of שש... and the mitre of שש, and the adorning mitres of שש, and the בד trousers of twined שש.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a פסוק in שמות. In this פסוק the word linen is repeated many times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said 'linen' once for all the garments. The repetition is the raw material that the next step will interpret.

phrases.english: As the verse states:
'And they made the tunics of linen...'
'and the mitre of linen,'
'and the adorning hats of linen,'
'and the linen trousers of twined linen.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by citing the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק in שמות that repeats the word linen.

steps.title: Five mentions, five lessons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counts five mentions of linen in the פסוק and assigns a separate lesson to each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five mentions are written. One is for the basic rule, that the garments are linen. One teaches that the thread is six-fold. One teaches that the strands are twisted together. One extends this to other garments where שש is not stated. One teaches that this is essential.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the repeated word teaches the six-strand rule. Each extra mention of linen is used for its own law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the first mention is needed to tell us the material is linen. The extra mentions add the six-strand rule, the twisting, the extension to other garments, and the rule that without these the garments are invalid (לעכב).

keyTerms.meaning: To be essential; without it the item is invalid

steps.whatToRemember: The extra mentions of שש teach that priestly linen threads must be six strands twisted together, for all the garments, and that this is essential.

phrases.english: Five mentions are written:
One for itself, that they should be linen.
And one, that their thread should be six-fold.
And one, that they should be twisted together.
And one, for the other garments
about which shesh is not stated.
And one, to make it indispensable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the quoted פסוק yields the rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each of the five mentions teaches a separate law, one of which is the six-strand rule.

steps.title: How do we know שש means linen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows that the word שש refers to linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it understood that this word שש means linen?
steps.whatsHappening: The previous step assumed that שש means linen. Now the גמרא asks for proof of that assumption, which sets up the next answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שש does not obviously name a material. The first use of the word ('for itself, that they are linen') depends on knowing what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: What indicates? How is it implied?

phrases.english: What indicates that this 'shesh' is linen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption from step 11 that שש means linen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the term שש means linen.

steps.title: The word בד: growing stalk by stalk
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא proves the point from the word בד, which describes a plant that grows one stalk at a time, like flax.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: the verse says 'בד', meaning something that grows from the ground stalk by stalk.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers. The same garments are also called בד, and בד means a plant growing as separate single stalks, which describes flax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שש and בד are used for the same garments, they mean the same material. בד is read as 'alone', meaning each stalk grows separately, which fits flax.

keyTerms.meaning: That grows up from the ground

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
As the verse says 'bad' —
something that grows from the ground
stalk by stalk, each one alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בד, which is interchangeable with שש, means something growing stalk by stalk, which is flax.

steps.title: Maybe it means wool
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: wool also grows hair by hair, so maybe בד means wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it means wool!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's proof. Each strand of wool also grows separately, so the description could fit wool too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'growing one by one' fits wool as well, the proof does not single out linen.

phrases.english: But say it means wool!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'growing stalk by stalk' points only to linen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wool also grows strand by strand, so the description is not unique to flax.

steps.title: Wool splits apart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that wool hairs split into several strands, so wool does not really grow one by one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wool splits apart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof. Each wool hair divides into smaller hairs, so it does not fit 'one stalk alone'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בד means each unit stays single. Wool naturally branches, so the description excludes it.

phrases.english: Wool splits apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction between the two materials
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wool grows strand by strand just like flax.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wool hairs naturally split, so they are not 'single'.

steps.title: Flax splits too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that flax also splits into fibers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Flax also splits!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Flax stalks also break into many fibers, so splitting cannot be the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both materials split, the distinction from the previous step falls apart.

phrases.english: Flax also splits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction that wool splits and flax does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flax also separates into fibers, so splitting does not distinguish the two.

steps.title: Flax splits only when beaten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that flax splits only when it is beaten, not by its natural growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Flax splits only through its beating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge. Flax grows as a single stalk and separates only after people process it, while wool splits naturally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key is how the material grows. Flax grows single and splits only by human processing, so the description בד בד fits flax and the proof stands.
steps.whatToRemember: בד means a plant growing as single stalks. Flax fits this because it splits only when beaten, unlike wool, which splits naturally.

phrases.english: Flax splits only through its being beaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16, confirming רבי יוסי's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes natural splitting from splitting caused by processing
steps.terutzMaskana: Flax splits only when beaten, so in its natural growth it is single.

steps.title: רבינא's proof from יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a different proof: יחזקאל calls these same priestly garments פשתים, which clearly means linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: from here: 'They shall have linen (פשתים) hats on their heads and linen trousers on their loins.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a second way to prove that שש means linen. He uses a פסוק in יחזקאל that describes the same garments with the plain word for linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פשתים clearly means flax or linen. Since יחזקאל uses it for the same hats and trousers the תורה calls שש and בד, those words must also mean linen, with no need for the stalk-by-stalk argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proof is more direct than the previous one, because it does not depend on how a plant grows.

phrases.english: Ravina said: from here:
'Linen hats shall be on their heads'
'and linen trousers shall be on their loins.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יחזקאל calls the same garments פשתים, which means linen, so שש means linen.

steps.title: Before יחזקאל, how was this known?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רבינא's proof from יחזקאל. If the law about linen garments is learned from יחזקאל, how did anyone know it before he came?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: But before יחזקאל came, who said this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the proof that רבינא just brought from the book of יחזקאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The priestly garments were made and worn in the משכן long before יחזקאל lived. If the only source for using linen is a verse in יחזקאל, then the earlier generations would have had no source at all. That seems impossible, so the proof looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: who said it? (who was the source?)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to him (to Ravina):
But before Ezekiel came,
who said it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִקַּמֵּי דְּאָתֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל, מַאן אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from יחזקאל brought in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's proof from the word פשתים in יחזקאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law that was kept in the משכן from the time of משה cannot depend on a prophet who lived centuries later.

steps.title: רבינא points to the same problem in רב חסדא's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers with 'ולטעמיך': the same question applies to רב חסדא, who said the law against an uncircumcised כהן serving is learned only from יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, what about רב חסדא's statement: 'This matter we did not learn from the Torah of משה רבינו. We learned it from the words of יחזקאל בן בוזי: No foreigner, uncircumcised of heart or uncircumcised of flesh, shall enter My sanctuary.' There too, before יחזקאל came, who said it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא turns רב אשי's question around and shows that it would also hit an accepted teaching of רב חסדא. This prepares the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא openly says that one law, the ban on an uncircumcised כהן serving, comes from יחזקאל and not from the Torah of משה. Nobody doubts that this law was kept before יחזקאל. So רב אשי's question cannot be a real reason to reject רבינא's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to your reasoning (turning the question back on the asker)
a foreigner (here understood as one whose actions are estranged from ה׳)

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying that רב חסדא's law did not exist before יחזקאל. He is showing that רב אשי's question proves too much, because it would also cancel a law everyone accepts.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, that which Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ,
phrases.english: This matter we did not learn from the Torah of Moses our teacher;
we learned it from the words of Ezekiel son of Buzi:
"No foreigner, uncircumcised of heart

phrases.aramaic: וְעֶרֶל בָּשָׂר לֹא יָבֹא אֶל מִקְדָּשִׁי״ —
phrases.english: or uncircumcised of flesh, shall enter My sanctuary" —

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִקַּמֵּי דְּאָתֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל, מַאן אַמְרַהּ?
phrases.english: there too, before Ezekiel came, who said it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רב אשי's question back on him to defend the proof from step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same question would wrongly cancel רב חסדא's accepted law, so the question itself must be flawed.

steps.title: It was a tradition, and יחזקאל attached it to a verse
steps.stepSummary: Both laws were known from an oral tradition, and יחזקאל later supported them with a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they had it as a received tradition, and יחזקאל came and attached it to a verse. Here too, they had it as a received tradition, and יחזקאל came and attached it to a verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered: the law was always known by tradition, and יחזקאל only gave it a verse to lean on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A law does not have to begin with a written verse. It can be handed down orally from משה, and a later prophet can attach it to a verse. This works for רב חסדא's law, and in the same way for the linen garments. So רבינא's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: they learned it as a received oral tradition
he attached (supported) it on a verse

steps.whatToRemember: A הלכה can come from oral tradition (גמרא גמירי לה), with a later prophet such as יחזקאל only giving it a supporting verse (אסמכתא). This defends רבינא's proof that שש means linen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key principle about how נביאים relate to Torah law. A prophet cannot create new Torah law, but he can anchor an existing tradition in a verse.

phrases.english: Rather, they learned it as a tradition,
and Ezekiel came and supported it with a verse.
Here too: they learned it as a tradition,
and Ezekiel came and supported it with a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גְּמָרָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ, וַאֲתָא יְחֶזְקֵאל וְאַסְמְכַהּ אַקְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer that removes the difficulty raised in step 19 and pointed out again in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the role of the source: the verse is a support for a tradition, not where the law begins
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The law comes only from the verse in יחזקאל, so it could not have existed before him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The law was an ancient tradition, and יחזקאל only attached it to a verse.

steps.title: Where do we learn that 'twisted' means eight strands?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's statement that משזר means thread spun from eight strands, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Twisted' (משזר) means eight. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the ברייתא and asks for the source of the number eight. This sets up the derivation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the threads described as משזר have eight strands. The Torah never states a number for this, so the גמרא needs to show where the number comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: twisted / spun together (thread made of several strands)
from where do we know this?

phrases.english: "Twisted" means eight.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by analyzing the next clause of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the pomegranate threads being eight strands each.

steps.title: Learning from the פרוכת with a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The word משזר appears both by the pomegranates and by the פרוכת. The פרוכת has 24 strands, so the pomegranates also have 24. Since they use three colors, each color is 8 strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And they made on the hem of the robe pomegranates of תכלת, ארגמן, and תולעת שני, twisted.' We learn 'twisted' from 'twisted' by the פרוכת. Just as there it is 24, so too here it is 24, so each one was eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה: the shared word משזר links the pomegranates to the פרוכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרוכת was made of four materials of six strands each, totaling 24. The pomegranates also need 24 strands in total. Because they have only three materials, the 24 is divided by three, so each thread has eight strands.

keyTerms.meaning: and he derives (here by גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: As it is written: "And they made upon the hem of the robe
pomegranates of sky-blue and purple
and scarlet, twisted";
and he derives "twisted" from "twisted" of the curtain:
phrases.notes: A גזירה שוה based on the shared word.

phrases.english: just as there it is twenty-four,
so too here it is twenty-four,
so that each one was eight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of משזר from the פרוכת gives 24 strands in total, divided among three colors, so eight each.

steps.title: Why not learn from the חושן and אפוד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we do not learn from the חושן and אפוד, which have 28 strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from the חושן and אפוד instead: just as there it is 28, so too here it should be 28!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of the פרוכת and suggests a different source that would give a different number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חושן and אפוד are also described as משזר, but they add gold threads, for a total of 28 strands. If we learned from them, the pomegranates would need 28 strands, not 24. So the question is why the פרוכת was chosen.

keyTerms.meaning: the breastplate of the כהן גדול
the apron of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: But let us derive it from the breastplate and ephod:
just as there it is twenty-eight,
so too here it should be twenty-eight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 23 by offering a competing source for the comparison.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the פרוכת as the source of the גזירה שוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word משזר also appears by the חושן and אפוד, which would give a different total of 28.

steps.title: Learn something without gold from something without gold
steps.stepSummary: The pomegranates have no gold, and neither does the פרוכת. So we learn from the פרוכת and not from the חושן and אפוד, which have gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn something for which gold is not stated from something for which gold is not stated. That excludes the חושן and אפוד, for which gold is stated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the choice of the פרוכת: it is more similar to the pomegranates because neither one contains gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When several sources share a word, we learn from the one most similar to our case. Gold is the very thing that makes the חושן and אפוד reach 28 strands. So a case without gold should be learned from a source without gold.

phrases.aramaic: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ זָהָב,
phrases.english: We derive an item for which gold is not stated
from an item for which gold is not stated,
to exclude the breastplate and ephod,
for which gold is stated.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by showing the פרוכת is the more similar source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing the closer comparison (similarity in having no gold)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חושן and אפוד are an equally good source, giving 28.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פרוכת is preferred because, like the pomegranates, it has no gold.

steps.title: On the contrary, learn a garment from a garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the pomegranates are part of a garment, so we should learn from the garments (חושן and אפוד), not from the פרוכת, which is part of the tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! We should learn a garment from a garment. That would exclude the פרוכת, which is part of the tent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues that a different similarity is more important, which would undo the previous answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a garment is also a strong similarity. The pomegranates are on the מעיל, a garment, and so are the חושן and אפוד. The פרוכת is part of the משכן structure, so by this standard it is the weaker match. The two similarities now point in opposite directions.

phrases.english: On the contrary: we should derive a garment from a garment,
to exclude the curtain — for it is part of the tent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 25 by raising a competing similarity.
steps.kashyaTarget: The preference for the פרוכת based on its having no gold
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being a garment is a stronger likeness, and that favors the חושן and אפוד over the פרוכת.

steps.title: The final source: the אבנט, a garment without gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that we learn from the אבנט. It is a garment and has no gold, so it matches the pomegranates in both ways and gives 24 strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from the אבנט. We learn a garment that has no stated gold from a garment that has no stated gold. And we do not learn something without gold from something with gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the debate by finding a source that has both features: the אבנט is a garment and contains no gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אבנט is made of four materials, totaling 24 strands, with no gold. Because it shares both features with the pomegranates, it beats the פרוכת (not a garment) and the חושן and אפוד (which have gold). So the total stays 24, which means eight strands for each of the three colors.

keyTerms.meaning: the belt worn by the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: The eight strands of each pomegranate thread are learned from the אבנט: a garment without gold (24 total ÷ 3 colors = 8). When comparing sources, we choose the one that matches our case in the most important ways.

phrases.english: Rather: we derive it from the belt,

phrases.aramaic: וְדָנִין בֶּגֶד וְדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ זָהָב,
phrases.english: and we derive a garment and an item for which gold is not stated

phrases.aramaic: מִבֶּגֶד וְדָבָר שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ זָהָב,
phrases.english: from a garment and an item for which gold is not stated,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ זָהָב
phrases.english: and we do not derive an item that has no gold
from an item that has gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 26 and replaces the פרוכת with the אבנט, which answers both concerns.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The pomegranate threads total 24 strands, eight per color, learned from the אבנט because it is both a garment and has no gold.

steps.title: רב מרי: The word תעשנו limits 28 strands to the חושן
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי gives another reason not to learn the pomegranates from the חושן and אפוד. The word תעשנו, written about the חושן, means the 28-strand rule is only for the חושן and not for anything else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: The verse writes 'תעשנו' (you shall make it). This means: make it this way for this item, and not for anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי gives a different reason why the pomegranates cannot copy the 28 strands of the חושן and אפוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the חושן says 'כמעשה אפוד תעשנו', meaning make it like the work of the אפוד. The extra word 'it' (תעשנו) tells us the 28-strand pattern belongs to the חושן alone. So no other item, including the pomegranates, can learn from it.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall make it. The word 'it' limits the rule to this one item.
For this one, and not for another

phrases.english: Rav Mari said:
'You shall make it' is written.
phrases.notes: Exodus 28:15, about the חושן: 'like the work of the אפוד you shall make it'.

phrases.english: You shall make it this way for this one, and not for another.
phrases.notes: The 28-strand thread is limited to the חושן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, besides the אבנט answer in Step 27, to the question of Step 24: why not learn from the חושן and אפוד?
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the pomegranates should have 28 strands, like the חושן and אפוד, since they are all garments.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word תעשנו limits the 28-strand rule to the חושן alone, so the pomegranates cannot learn from it.

steps.title: רב אשי: The word ועשית means all the colors must be equal
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a third reason. The word ועשית, written about the pomegranates, teaches that every colored thread must have the same number of strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The verse writes 'ועשית' (and you shall make). This teaches that all the parts of it must be made equal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own reason why the pomegranates cannot have 28 strands. He starts by stating a rule from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pomegranates are made of three colors: תכלת, ארגמן, and תולעת שני. The word ועשית teaches that each color must have the same number of strands. In the next lines, the גמרא will show that 28 cannot be split this way.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall make (Exodus 28:33, about the pomegranates)
Equal makings, meaning each color thread has the same number of strands

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
'And you shall make' is written,
phrases.notes: Exodus 28:33: 'And you shall make pomegranates of תכלת, ארגמן, and תולעת שני'.

phrases.english: so that all the makings will be equal.
phrases.notes: Each color must use the same number of strands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of Step 24, offered alongside רב מרי's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rule from the verse that blocks the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the pomegranates could have 28 strands, like the חושן and אפוד.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three colors must be equal, and 28 cannot be split equally into three. The גמרא proves this in the next steps.

steps.title: How could 28 be split? Three threads of 10 make 30
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests רב אשי's point. It asks how we could split 28 strands among three colors. The first try, three threads of 10 each, adds up to 30, which is too many.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how should we make it? Should we make three threads of ten strands each? That would be thirty, not twenty-eight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins checking whether 28 strands can be divided equally among the three colors. The first attempt fails because it gives the wrong total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each color has 10 strands, the total is 30, not 28. So equal threads of 10 do not work. This sets up the next attempt, which uses unequal threads.

keyTerms.meaning: And how should we do it?

phrases.english: And how should we do it?
Let us make three threads of ten strands each —
they would be thirty!
phrases.notes: That is too many, since the total should be 28.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out רב אשי's rule with numbers and tries the first possible split of 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a way to divide 28 strands into three colors?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three threads of 10 each gives 30, so that does not work.

steps.title: Splitting into 9, 9, and 10 breaks the rule that the colors must be equal
steps.stepSummary: The second try is 9, 9, and 10, which does add up to 28. But the verse ועשית requires all the colors to be equal, so this is rejected. Therefore the pomegranates cannot have 28 strands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we make two threads of nine strands each and one of ten? The verse says 'ועשית', which teaches that all its makings must be equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the only split that adds up to 28 and rejects it, because the colors would not be equal. This completes רב אשי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 9 + 9 + 10 = 28, so the total is correct. But the threads would not be equal, and ועשית demands that they be equal. Since 28 cannot be divided evenly by three, the pomegranates must learn from an item whose number divides by three, such as the פרוכת or אבנט with 24 strands.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to why the pomegranates are not learned from the חושן and אפוד: (1) learn from the אבנט, a garment with no gold, which has 24; (2) רב מרי: תעשנו limits 28 to the חושן; (3) רב אשי: ועשית requires three equal colors, and 28 cannot be split into three equal parts.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the problem with 9-9-10 is the total. The total is exactly 28. The only problem is that the three colors are not equal.

phrases.english: Let us make two threads of nine strands each
and one of ten —
the verse says: 'And you shall make,'
so that all its makings will be equal.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶעְבֵּיד תְּרֵי דְּתִשְׁעָה תִּשְׁעָה וְחַד דְּעַשְׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first split fails in Step 30, this tries the second split and rejects it using רב אשי's verse.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 9-9-10 split, and with it the idea that the pomegranates could have 28 strands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The threads would be unequal, which goes against ועשית, the rule that all the makings must be equal.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the מעיל has 12 strands?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next part of the ברייתא: the threads of the מעיל are made of 12 strands. It asks for the source and begins quoting a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מעיל has twelve strands. From where do we know this? As it is written: 'And you shall make the robe of the אפוד'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the source for the 12 strands of the מעיל. It is starting to bring the proof, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about the pomegranates on the hem. Now the topic is the מעיל itself. The גמרא starts quoting Exodus 28:31 as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: The robe worn by the כהן גדול
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The robe is twelve strands. From where do we know this?
As it is written: 'And you shall make the robe of the ephod
phrases.notes: Exodus 28:31. The verse and the proof continue on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The pomegranate discussion is finished. The גמרא moves on to the next detail of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that the threads of the מעיל are made of 12 strands?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גמרא begins to answer from the פסוק 'ועשית את מעיל האפוד'. The full explanation continues on the next amud.
